## cargoship dev clean-cache

Reports what the shared cache holds, and removes it

### Synopsis

Reports every area of the shared cache with its size, then removes the content a build can fetch again. Nothing else reclaims it: the cache has no size limit and no expiry, so it grows for as long as definitions name new versions.

What is removed is content, not record. The downloaded files and the archives extracted from them, the image blobs, and the examples generator's assets all come back on the next run that wants them, at the cost of fetching them again. The run logs and the local dev fleet's base images are left alone: nothing regenerates a log, and a fleet image is a multi-gigabyte download owned by 'mage dev:vmImage' rather than by a package build.

Pass --older-than to keep the working set and drop what a definition has stopped naming, which is usually what is wanted on a machine still in use. Note that it cannot prune an image layout: that area is an index over shared blobs, so removing some of them by age would leave the index naming blobs that are gone. It is reported as skipped, and comes out whole when --older-than is not given.

An entry's age is when it was written, not when it was last used, so a long-lived entry still in use can fall outside the window and be fetched again. This changes nothing but the time the next build takes.

Nothing here touches a cluster or a host. Use --dry-run to see what would go.

```
cargoship dev clean-cache [flags]
```

### Examples

```

# Report what the cache holds and what would be removed, removing nothing
$ cargoship dev clean-cache --dry-run

# Remove every fetchable thing in it
$ cargoship dev clean-cache

# Keep anything fetched in the last fortnight
$ cargoship dev clean-cache --older-than 336h

```

### Options

```
      --dry-run[=true|false]   Report what would be removed without removing it.
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for clean-cache
      --older-than duration    Only remove entries written longer ago than this Go duration, such as 336h. Omit to remove every fetchable area.
      --zarf-cache string      Specify the location of the Zarf cache directory (default "$HOME/.cache/cargoship")
```
